label: lem:antideriv_diff_zero_deriv
title: Difference of antiderivatives has zero derivative
statement: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that $F$ and $G$ are both antiderivatives of $f$ on $(a,b)$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:antiderivative}. Then the difference function $F - G$ has derivative zero at every point $x \in (a,b)$. That is, $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; (F - G)\; 0\; x$ holds for every $x \in (a,b)$.
proof: Fix $x \in (a,b)$. By Definition~\ref{def:antiderivative}, both $F$ and $G$ satisfy $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; F\; (f\; x)\; x$ and $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; (f\; x)\; x$ respectively. By the linearity of the derivative (specifically \texttt{HasDerivAt.sub}), the difference $F - G$ has derivative $f(x) - f(x) = 0$ at $x$.
